summary: Iteration 135 regression of the iter134 canonical/backend hardening, run against an isolated real Mongo DB (tejas_isolated_iter134). Every tejas/server Motor handle was rebound (leftover check came back empty). No lifespan ran, so no seed_owner, worker or AI. Production indexes() were built only after rebinding. The DB was dropped after each run and no isolated DB is left. Result: 49 of 50 new isolated tests pass. All 5 iter134 faults that had strict xfail markers are now fixed and pass with unchanged invariants: app-clock skew sealing; finalize(time_limit) on a future deadline; PDF source SHA check; limiter DuplicateKeyError; cold pack amplification. The one failure is a NEW fault: exam-navigation history leaks an embargoed summary when the app clock is ahead. Auth regression: iter118 auth/CORS/lockout passed 75 with 4 skipped, iter118 origins unit passed 75, iter119 denied headers passed 18. Older isolated suites: iter109 15/15, iter122 39/39, iter123 43/43, iter121 33/33 after a test-only namespace fix; iter116 not run because it needs its legacy bridge. Frontend was tested in a real browser against the preview frontend, with /api routed to an isolated ASGI bridge and mocked auth/session, at 1920x800 and 390x844. Deadline confirmation via /status, clock resync, 503 retry, navigation on completion and the ?late=true pending-draft flag all work. The production build (BUILD_PATH=/tmp, removed afterwards) compiled with lint warnings only. No customer writes, real logins, AI runs or storage uploads. No 500k capacity claim is made.

minor.issue: NEW FAULT (test fails): embargo and expiry are compared against the app clock now(), not the DB clock. With the app clock +3600s and a DB competition_end 1800s in the future, the embargoed summary is returned ({'score':4} leaked). The same pattern exists in cohorts.py:64,142 (cohort embargo), ai_solutions.py:82 (worked-solution embargo), jobs.py:251 (report download embargo), learning_progress.py:77, and the display-only status override in chapter_books.py:283 and exam_navigation.py:104, which shows 'completed' while the attempt is active in the DB. finalize() is DB-guarded, so nothing seals early; the risk is early release of embargoed data and wrong status labels under skew.

The real drain query uses kind_1_status_1_next_run_at_1_created_at_1 but needs a blocking in-memory SORT on created_at, because next_run_at is a $expr range ahead of created_at in the index. Each drain iteration (16 per release) re-sorts the whole queued backlog of that kind.
The output fields use $literal but 'message' does not. A process()/refresh() message starting with '$' would be read as a field path inside the pipeline update. Wrap it in {'$literal': message}.
get(attempts) loads the full attempt document, including command_receipts, for grading. A lightweight projection would reduce memory and IO.
By design, 16 of 32 concurrent full attempt reads on one process get 503 (read limit 16). The frontend retries with backoff, but a class starting together will see some busy errors.

ui_bugs.issue: After a /status 503, the error banner stays visible even after a later /status call succeeds (200 active), because the success path never calls setError(''). Seen 9s after recovery in the 1920 screenshot.

issues: A long unbroken receipt id overflows horizontally (scrollWidth 435 vs 390). This was seen with a synthetic 43-character id; real UUIDs have hyphens and may wrap, but overflow-wrap:anywhere on the receipt line would be more robust.
The save indicator shows a check icon next to '1 pending · not yet acknowledged', which sends a mixed signal.

rca of the issue: Embargo leak: the hardening moved attempts.py (owned/clocked_one/_database_now) and attempt_status to the Mongo $$NOW clock, but the satellite read models in exam_navigation, cohorts, ai_solutions, jobs.download and learning_progress still call tejas.db.now() (app clock). Reproduction: completed attempt with competition_end = real+1800 and app clock offset +3600; GET /api/exam-navigation/jee-main/history returns the summary. Fix: project _database_now via EPOCH_NOW in those aggregations, or compare inside the query with $expr.
